_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); gold-miner signals with Newmont's rule-T thresholds

pit_profile.why: 'Newmont is one of the world’s largest gold producers and is the only gold company included in the S&P 500 Index and the Fortune 500, and has been included in the Dow Jones Sustainability Index-World for six consecutive years.' 'Our business is dependent on the prices of gold and copper, which fluctuate on a daily basis and are affected by numerous factors beyond our control.' 'A substantial or extended decline in gold or copper prices would have a material adverse effect on Newmont.' (the FY2012 10-K's own words; it does not call the business cyclical, so DURABLE, the MU rule); no disruption theme in the registry is live for a gold miner on this date (of the live themes, OFFSHORE is scoped to 'lower-cost offshore delivery (Indian IT services) takes share and price from Western consulting, systems integration and outsourcing', CLOUD to 'public cloud displaces on-premise hardware, storage, legacy databases and data-center outsourcing': none names a miner), so the watch list is empty

'A substantial or extended decline in gold or copper prices would have a material adverse effect on Newmont.' (the FY2012 10-K's own words; it does not call the business cyclical, so DURABLE, the MU rule); no disruption theme in the registry is live for a gold miner on this date (of the live themes, OFFSHORE is scoped to 'lower-cost offshore delivery (Indian IT services) takes share and price from Western consulting, systems integration and outsourcing', CLOUD to 'public cloud displaces on-premise hardware, storage, legacy databases and data-center outsourcing': none names a miner), so the watch list is empty. durable franchise (obsolescence risk 2/5); price cheap; Ratio B 0.04x; -52% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap +1.18; conservative 2yr +179%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -36.2%/yr (worst year FY03-FY12 ex-FY07 ex-FY11, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS -22.1%/yr (Q3 revenue YoY + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr ex-FY07 ex-FY11 median

BULL.desc: EPS +16.7%/yr (FY03-FY12 ex-FY07 ex-FY11 CAGR, at least BASE); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +60.0%/yr (best 2-yr run FY03-FY12 ex-FY07 ex-FY11, at least BULL); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: NEM (retrospective, 2013-12-27) ◉ BUY — Ratio B 0.04x (33.4% downside to Bear $15.71 / +871.5% upside to Bull $229.18) | Adj composite 2.40 vs market 1.22: gap +1.18 [UNDERVALUED] | -52% above the EPP floor $49.14 (13x FY13E $3.78) | Conservative 2-yr case: +179.4% total (+89.7%/yr) | At 6.2x FY13E the 15% hurdle price $31.20 sits at or below the BASE case; revenue -20.0% YoY in Q3 2013, forward revenues -20% (Q3 2013 revenue growth (no revenue guide)); no disruption theme has dated evidence.
